subject: general
question: The tops of two poles of heights 18 m and 30.5 m are connected by a wire. If the wire makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal, what is the length (in m) of the wire?
solution:
Given:

The tops of two poles of heights 18 m and 30.5 m are connected by a wire. 

The wire makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal.

**Concept used:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/894f5ee455905e7c8653ae85bb8d1afcd0a4fd4f6ed9e1e07d3cf4cdebe1b0ab.png] 

ΔABC is a right-angled triangle at B, SinA = CB/CA

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a5b1d4c013ba48593ecefffec281fc4d35d5aabb012b4ee9d0e2ecec2607aad.png] 

Calculation:

Let AB and CD be the towers of heights 30.5 and 18 m respectively and AC be the wire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3cc3bfca82a30add73cd4f3aad68d840f46db05112e74300402d39c458ffb00c.png] 

Here, CD = EB = 18 m and CE = DB

So, AE = 30.5 - 18 = 12.5 m

ΔAEC is a right-angled triangle at E. 

sin 30° = AE/AC

⇒ 1/2 = 12.5/AC

⇒ AC = 25

∴ The length of the wire is 25 m.
